title: FMGE PSM Day 4 Mock
subject: Community Medicine
description: A 38-question PSM mock from the reviewed Day 4 notes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a qualitative variable?
questions.explanation: Religion is a qualitative variable; weight is quantitative.

questions.stem: A cancer variable records stages I, II, III and IV. Which scale applies?
questions.explanation: Ordered categories use an ordinal scale. Nominal categories classify by name without an inherent order.

questions.stem: The scatter plot shown indicates:
questions.image_alt: Scatter plot showing the relationship between X and Y
questions.image_source: p.32 | upper-left scatter plot only, cropped before the handwritten correlation labels
questions.explanation: An upward scatter pattern indicates positive correlation. No correlation produces no consistent upward or downward relationship.

questions.stem: Mean haemoglobin is compared across four independent treatment groups with normally distributed values and equal variances. Which test is appropriate?
questions.explanation: ANOVA compares means across three or more independent groups when quantitative data are normally distributed. An unpaired t-test is for two independent groups.

questions.stem: Two independent random samples have the same SD: A has n=25 and B has n=100. Which statement about the standard error of the mean is correct?
options: A has half the SE of B
B has half the SE of A and is more precise
B has twice the SE of A and is less precise
questions.explanation: SE equals SD divided by √n, so increasing n from 25 to 100 halves the SE. Lower SE means greater precision.
questions.answer_label: B has half the SE of A and is more precise
questions.answer: B has half the SE of A and is more precise

questions.stem: The nonsteroidal oral contraceptives Saheli and Chhaya contain:
questions.explanation: Saheli/Chhaya is the nonsteroidal oral contraceptive ormeloxifene; it is not raloxifene.

questions.stem: A chi-square test uses a 3 × 4 contingency table. Degrees of freedom?
questions.explanation: For a 3 × 4 table, degrees of freedom are (3−1)(4−1)=6. Eight results from using four instead of three for the column factor.

questions.stem: Which IUD belongs to the first generation?
questions.explanation: Lippes Loop is a first-generation nonmedicated IUD. CuT 7 belongs to a different generation.

questions.stem: A trial concludes a new drug is superior, but in reality it is not. Which error occurred?
questions.explanation: Concluding superiority when the null of no superiority is actually true means rejecting a true null hypothesis: Type I error. Type II error means failing to reject a false null hypothesis.

questions.stem: The basal body temperature rise used for ovulation detection occurs during the:
questions.explanation: The basal body temperature rise occurs after ovulation; the preovulatory phase precedes this temperature shift.

questions.stem: A woman records cycle dates, basal temperature and cervical mucus to avoid fertile days. Which method is she using?
questions.explanation: Combining cycle dates, basal body temperature and cervical mucus is the symptothermal method. BBT alone uses only one component.

questions.stem: Pain is graded mild, moderate or severe in the same patients before and after therapy. Investigators compare the numbers who improve and worsen, excluding ties. Which test is appropriate?
questions.explanation: The sign test compares the directions of change in paired ordinal observations, excluding ties. A paired t-test analyzes quantitative within-pair differences; skewness of the original before and after measurements alone does not establish that its assumptions fail.

questions.stem: Toxic shock syndrome is a recognized complication of which barrier contraceptive?
questions.explanation: Toxic shock syndrome is a recognized complication of the vaginal sponge. Male condoms are barrier contraception, but they do not share this association.

questions.stem: A woman using a combined OCP asks about adverse effects. Which risk is increased?
questions.explanation: Combined OCPs are associated with increased thromboembolism, whereas ovarian cysts are among the effects shown to decrease.

questions.stem: All of the following are among the 4As of primary health care EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Acceptable, accessible, available and affordable form the 4As; achievable is not one of them.

questions.stem: Use of ORS at primary-care level illustrates which PHC principle?
questions.explanation: ORS is an example of appropriate technology in primary health care. Community participation is a separate PHC principle.

questions.stem: In India’s rural public health system, the most peripheral health facility is the:
questions.explanation: The subcentre is the most peripheral unit for health-care delivery. A PHC remains a primary-level facility but is not the most peripheral.

questions.stem: In village health work, an ASHA commonly links community members with which frontline health worker?
questions.explanation: ASHA links village residents with the auxiliary nurse midwife (ANM) and the broader public health system, including Anganwadi, subcentre and PHC services.

questions.stem: Which rural health facility generally provides secondary referral care above the PHC level?
questions.explanation: A CHC provides secondary referral care above the PHC level. A designated First Referral Unit must meet additional service requirements; not every CHC is an FRU.

questions.stem: A woman wants a nonhormonal IUD that can remain in use for 10 years. Best option?
questions.explanation: CuT 380A is a copper, nonhormonal IUD approved for up to 10 years in India’s family-planning programme. CuT 375 is approved for up to 5 years.

questions.stem: At block level, which Panchayati Raj institution corresponds to the administrative tier in the hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Panchayat Samiti corresponds to block level, while Zila Parishad is the district-level tier.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT included in AYUSH?
questions.explanation: AYUSH includes Sowa-Rigpa; allopathy is outside this grouping.

questions.stem: A painter develops abdominal colic, a Burtonian gum line and wrist drop. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Burtonian line with abdominal colic and wrist drop forms the classic clinical cluster for lead poisoning. The competing poisonings do not match this combination.

questions.stem: A textile worker exposed to cotton dust is at risk of:
questions.explanation: Cotton-fibre exposure is linked to byssinosis. Mouldy-hay exposure is linked to farmer's lung.

questions.stem: A dye-industry worker exposed to aromatic amines such as benzidine develops painless hematuria. Most likely occupational malignancy?
questions.explanation: Occupational exposure to carcinogenic aromatic amines used in dye production, including benzidine, increases the risk of urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma of the bladder.

questions.stem: Mesothelioma is classically associated with occupational exposure to:
questions.explanation: Asbestos exposure is associated with mesothelioma. Coal dust is linked to a different pneumoconiosis.

questions.stem: A woman receives Antara. When should her next injection be scheduled?
questions.explanation: Antara is depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA). The routine repeat-injection interval is 3 months.

questions.stem: In the demographic cycle, birth rate remains high while death rate begins to fall. Which stage is this?
questions.explanation: Early expanding stage has a high birth rate with the death rate starting to fall. In late expanding stage, the birth rate also begins to decline.

questions.stem: Silicosis has a recognized association with:
questions.explanation: Silicosis is associated with tuberculosis. Aspergillus is paired with compost-lung exposure rather than silicosis.

questions.stem: A census counts each person at the place where they are physically present during enumeration. This method is:
questions.explanation: De facto census counts people at their actual location during data collection. The de jure alternative does not fit that location rule.

questions.stem: Occupational exposure to vinyl chloride monomer during PVC manufacture is associated with:
questions.explanation: Vinyl chloride monomer exposure during PVC manufacture is associated with hepatic angiosarcoma. The classic carcinogenic exposure is the monomer, rather than ordinary contact with finished PVC products.

questions.stem: Over one year, a district records 240 live births with 12,000 women aged 15–49 years at midyear. The annual GFR per 1,000 is:
questions.explanation: GFR is live births divided by women aged 15–49 years, multiplied by 1,000. Thus 240/12,000 × 1,000 = 20.

questions.stem: Occupational leukemia is classically associated with exposure to:
questions.explanation: Benzene exposure is associated with leukemia. Wood dust has a different occupational-cancer association.

questions.stem: A national vital-statistics system uses dual-record collection. Which indicator can it directly estimate?
questions.explanation: The dual-record system identifies SRS, which measures IMR among its vital indicators. Literacy rate belongs to a different demographic measurement context.

questions.stem: A population pyramid has a broad base, narrow top and shorter span. It most likely represents a:
questions.explanation: A developing population has an upright triangular pyramid with a broad base and narrow top. A developed population has a spindle-like profile with a middle bulge.

questions.stem: A population pyramid is graphically a:
questions.explanation: A population pyramid is a double histogram. A line chart is used for a temporal trend.

questions.stem: A town has 10,000 people, including 1,000 children under 7 years. The denominator for literacy rate is:
questions.explanation: Literacy rate uses the population aged 7 years and above. Excluding 1,000 children under 7 from 10,000 leaves a denominator of 9,000.

questions.stem: Sex ratio in the Census of India is calculated as:
options: Female live births / total live births × 1000
Girls aged 0–6 years / boys aged 0–6 years × 1000
questions.explanation: Sex ratio is females divided by males multiplied by 1,000. Restricting both groups to ages 0–6 gives the child sex ratio instead.
